extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, applicants for USPTO registration, OED staff, and legal counsel involved in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria governing approval of an Affidavit of Resignation and the exclusion on consent of a patent practitioner under USPTO disciplinary rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.27, § 11.25, § 11.60, etc.). Covers notice, required acknowledgements, alleged rule violations, publication, and reinstatement consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority to approve affidavit and exclude on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a person on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may approve an Affidavit of Resignation submitted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and impose exclusion on consent; the Final Order cites these statutory/regulatory bases as the authority for the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation content and acknowledgements (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Affidavit of Resignation must include certain acknowledgements demonstrated by the Respondent: that consent is freely and voluntarily rendered (no coercion/duress); awareness of investigations and allegations; knowledge of applicable USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and related regulations (e.g., 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, 11.60); acknowledgment of consequences of consenting to exclusion; consent to being excluded; and, if later applying for reinstatement, recognition that the OED Director may presume certain facts true for reinstatement purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds the Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' To be approved, the affidavit should expressly state the enumerated acknowledgements (free consent, awareness of investigations/allegations, understanding of consequences, consent to exclusion, and acceptance of reinstatement presumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension procedure and notice (37 C.F.R. § 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, the OED Director may request an interim suspension when there is evidence that the practitioner committed a serious crime; the Office issues a 'Notice and Order' providing the practitioner an opportunity to file a response within forty (40) days. Notice may be sent by certified mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document shows the Office sent a Notice and Order by certified mail (with tracking), provided a 40-day response window, and that failure to respond can result in imposition of interim discipline. This describes the procedural protections and timing that must be afforded before interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited practitioner conduct under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804 (subsections a, b, c, d, i)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804 provisions cited: (a) practitioner shall not violate or attempt to violate the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; (b) practitioner shall not commit a criminal act that reflects adversely on honesty, trustworthiness, or fitness as a practitioner; (c) practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation; (d) practitioner shall not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice; (i) practitioner shall not engage in conduct that adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director may opine that particular facts constitute violations of these provisions (and the affidavit may acknowledge those opinions). These are the primary behavioral standards by which practitioners' conduct is judged in disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant obligations and prohibitions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.801 (subsections a, b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801 provisions cited: (a) an applicant in connection with registration shall not knowingly make a false statement of material fact; (b) an applicant shall not fail to disclose a fact necessary to correct a misapprehension known by the person to have arisen in the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to be truthful or to correct a misapprehension in registration materials (e.g., moral character questions, data sheet) may constitute grounds for disciplinary action and can be asserted by OED in investigations or proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose criminal convictions and keep registration information current
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants/registrants must disclose criminal convictions and update moral character/information papers; failure to update information to reflect convictions occurring after submission (and failure to notify OED of such convictions as required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25) are alleged grounds for discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order details allegations that Respondent did not properly update moral character information received March 13, 2014 and failed to deliver required notice regarding later convictions. Registrants should timely update the OED and registration records and provide notices required by rule to avoid disciplinary allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and related presumptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person who consents to exclusion later applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director may conclusively presume, for the purpose of determining the reinstatement application, that the facts set forth in the OED investigations are true and that the person could not have successfully defended against the alleged violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Affidavit of Resignation may include an acknowledgment that these presumptions will apply on future reinstatement applications. The Final Order also commands compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement and compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations following exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided Notice of Exclusion on Consent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies both electronic publication and Official Gazette notice content/consistency requirements. Practitioners should expect public posting of disciplinary outcomes and that the Office will issue a standardized notice describing the exclusion and the underlying facts/opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration processing responsibilities (data sheet and name accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration requires submission of a Data Sheet (Register of Patent Attorneys and Agents) and may include requests to change/update the name under which an applicant is approved; registrants are responsible for ensuring the accuracy of public USPTO practitioner records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order recounts that Respondent passed the registration exam, the OED received the Data Sheet, and Respondent later requested a name update. Accurate Data Sheets and timely updates affect public records and may bear on OED investigations if inconsistencies arise.
